q: What is the standard size of a single bed?
n: Single bed: 0.90 × 1.90 m.
ref: Panero and Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space - beds and bedroom clearances; Neufert, Architects' Data, 5th ed.

q: What is the standard size of a twin bed?
n: Twin bed: 1.00 × 1.90 m.
ref: Panero and Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space - beds and bedroom clearances; Neufert, Architects' Data, 5th ed.

q: What is the standard size of a double bed?
n: Double bed: 1.35 × 1.90 m.
ref: Panero and Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space - beds and bedroom clearances; Neufert, Architects' Data, 5th ed.

q: What is the standard size of a queen bed?
n: Queen bed: 1.50 × 2.00 m.
ref: Panero and Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space - beds and bedroom clearances; Neufert, Architects' Data, 5th ed.

q: What is the standard size of a king bed?
n: King bed: 1.90 × 2.00 m.
ref: Panero and Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space - beds and bedroom clearances; Neufert, Architects' Data, 5th ed.

q: What is the recommended height of a bar stool?
n: Bar stool seats sit 0.70 to 0.80 m above the floor, to suit a bar counter 1.05 to 1.15 m high.
ref: Neufert, Architects' Data, 5th ed. - bar counters and stool heights

q: What is the least viewing distance from a 60-inch TV?
n: A 60-inch screen needs about 2.30 m of viewing distance at the near limit.
ref: Neufert, Architects' Data, 5th ed. - television and screen viewing distances

q: What is the maximum viewing distance from a 43-inch TV?
n: A 43-inch screen stays comfortable up to about 1.50 m at the far limit.
ref: Neufert, Architects' Data, 5th ed. - television and screen viewing distances

q: What is the area of a dining room for 8 persons, using Fajardo's planning handbook allowance?
n: Dining areas are sized at about 1.80 sqm per person, so 8 persons need 14.40 sqm.
ref: Fajardo, Planning and Designer's Handbook - dining room area per person

q: What is the minimum size of a dirty kitchen?
n: A dirty kitchen is planned at 3 sqm minimum for the service cooking area.
ref: Fajardo, Planning and Designer's Handbook - kitchen and service areas

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the maximum height of the lip of an accessible wall-hung urinal, measured from the toilet floor?
n: The 2024 Revised IRR sets the lip of a wall-hung accessible urinal at 350 to 400 mm above the toilet floor, with a clear level space of 900 x 900 mm in front. The 480 mm figure comes from the superseded 1983 IRR.
ref: BP 344, 2024 Revised IRR, Sec. 6.12 - accessible urinals

q: What is the minimum size of a car parking slot when it is perpendicular or diagonal to the aisle?
n: A perpendicular or diagonal car slot is 2.50 m wide by 5.00 m long.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VII Sec. 707 - off-street parking slot dimensions

q: What is the minimum size of a car parking slot when it is parallel to the aisle?
n: A parallel car slot is 2.15 m wide by 6.00 m long. A perpendicular slot is 2.50 m wide, so check which layout the question means.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VII Sec. 707 - off-street parking slot dimensions

q: What does MACA stand for?
n: MACA = PSO + ISA, the area of the lot that may be built or paved.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VII and Rule VIII - development controls

q: What does TOSL stand for, and how is it computed?
o: Total Occupied Site Level; TOSL = PSO + ISA
Total Open Site Line; TOSL = TLA − GFA
Total Open Space within Lot; TOSL = ISA + USA
Total Occupancy Space Limit; TOSL = USA − ISA
n: TOSL is the part of the lot not occupied by the building: the paved (ISA) plus unpaved (USA) open space.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VII and Rule VIII - development controls

q: What does USA stand for in development controls?
n: USA is the softscape: exposed, planted soil, and it is the true open space.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VII and Rule VIII - development controls

q: What does ISA stand for in development controls?
n: ISA is the paved or hardscaped open space, such as walkways and driveways.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VII and Rule VIII - development controls

q: What does PSO stand for, and how is it computed?
o: Percentage of Setback Occupancy; PSO = TOSL ÷ TLA
Percentage of Site Occupancy; PSO = AMBF ÷ TLA
Permitted Site Openings; PSO = GFA ÷ TLA
Projected Site Occupancy; PSO = ISA ÷ USA
n: PSO is the share of the lot the building may occupy at grade.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VII and Rule VIII - development controls

q: What does AMBF stand for, and how is it computed?
o: Allowable Maximum Building Frontage; AMBF = TLA × ISA
Average Maximum Building Floor; AMBF = GFA ÷ TLA
Allowable Maximum Building Footprint; AMBF = TLA × PSO
Allowable Minimum Building Footprint; AMBF = TLA − TOSL
n: AMBF is the largest ground-floor footprint after applying the PSO and the setback rules.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VII and Rule VIII - development controls

q: How is the maximum Gross Floor Area (GFA) of a lot computed?
n: FLAR is the Floor-to-Lot Area Ratio, so GFA is the lot area multiplied by that ratio.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VII and Rule VIII - development controls

q: A regular rectangular lot measures 16 m × 14.52 m. What is its Total Lot Area (TLA)?
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VII and Rule VIII - development controls (TLA computation)

q: What is the standard method for getting the area of an irregular lot given its bearings and distances?
o: Compute latitudes and departures, then apply the DMD or coordinate method
Average the bearings and multiply by the perimeter
Use the perimeter times the apothem
n: Plot the traverse, find the latitudes and departures, then compute the area by the double-meridian-distance or coordinate method.
ref: La Putt, Elementary Surveying - traverse area by latitudes and departures (DMD and coordinate methods)

q: Other subgroupings or divisions within Groups A to J may be determined by the ______.
n: Groups A to J are fixed by the Code, but the Secretary of the DPWH may set other subgroupings or divisions within them.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VII Sec. 701 - occupancy classification

q: The character of occupancy of existing buildings may be changed subject to the approval of the ______.
n: A change in the character of occupancy or use needs the approval of the Building Official, and the building must then meet the requirements of the new occupancy.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VII Sec. 702 - change in use or occupancy

q: No building shall be constructed unless it adjoins or has ______.
o: direct access to a public space, yard or street on at least one of its sides
direct access to a road with a 12 m right-of-way
an easement of at least 3 m on two sides
a private road on all sides
n: Every building must adjoin or have direct access to a public space, yard or street on at least one side, and must face a public street.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VIII, Streets and Road Right-of-Way, Sec. C.1

q: Every dwelling shall be provided with ______ and adequate washing and drainage facilities.
o: a septic tank and a cistern
one toilet and one bath per bedroom
n: Every dwelling must have at least one sanitary toilet plus adequate washing and drainage facilities.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VII Sec. 708.3 - sanitation, Group A dwellings

q: What is the minimum number of steps from the sidewalk to the ground floor level?
n: Entrance and exit steps from the sidewalk take a minimum of two steps, with treads of at least 300 mm.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VIII, Guidelines on Sidewalks and Arcades, Sec. 12.a.v - entrance and exit steps

q: What is the maximum riser height for the steps from the sidewalk to the ground floor level?
n: Risers on entrance and exit steps from the sidewalk may not exceed 100 mm.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VIII, Guidelines on Sidewalks and Arcades, Sec. 12.a.v - entrance and exit steps

q: Which of the following is NOT a type of lap pool step (Edge, Corner, Centered, Outward)?
n: Lap pool entry steps are described as edge, corner and outward types. Centered is not one of them.
ref: Neufert, Architects' Data, 5th ed. - swimming pools, entry steps

q: What width is allotted to a one-way passage for a single person walking?
n: A single walking person needs a 760 to 920 mm path, which covers body breadth plus clearance.
ref: Panero and Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space - circulation, single-file passage

q: What width is allotted to a two-way corridor where two persons pass each other?
n: Two persons passing need about 1500 mm of corridor width.
ref: Panero and Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space - circulation, two-person passage

q: Under the National Building Code, what is the minimum width of a corridor or exterior exit balcony?
n: Every corridor or exit balcony must be at least 1.10 m wide. Anthropometric comfort widths are larger, but 1.10 m is the legal minimum.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Means of Egress - corridors and exterior exit balconies

q: Two vans are parked one behind the other along a driveway, parallel to the aisle. What total length do they occupy?
n: A parallel parking slot is 6.00 m long, so two vehicles in line need 2 x 6.00 = 12.00 m. The same 12.00 m applies to a sedan behind a van or behind an SUV, since the slot length does not change with the vehicle.
steps: Two vehicles in line = 2 x 6.00 m
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VII Sec. 707 - off-street parking slot dimensions

q: What is the minimum tread of entrance or exit steps from the sidewalk?
n: Entrance and exit steps need treads of at least 300 mm, a minimum of two steps, and risers not over 100 mm. Two treads give a 600 mm total run.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VIII, Guidelines on Sidewalks and Arcades, Sec. 12.a.v - entrance and exit steps

q: In a multi-storey building, what is the minimum unobstructed head-room clearance above the finished floor of the upper storeys?
n: Ceiling heights run 2.70 m for the first storey and 2.40 m for the second, and the succeeding storeys need an unobstructed head-room clearance of at least 2.10 m.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VIII Sec. 805 - ceiling heights

q: What is the average floor area of a dental operatory, the treatment room holding one dental chair?
n: Operatories run from 8 x 10 ft to 10 x 12 ft, and 100 sq ft (about 9.3 sqm) is the average. A whole dental clinic adds reception, sterilizing, laboratory and x-ray areas on top of this.
ref: Time-Saver Standards for Building Types, 3rd ed. - Design of the Dental Operatory
